IN CR.NO.103/2021 OF WOMEN P.S., CHICKBALLAPURA FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S.363,
376(2)(n) OF IPC AND SEC.4 AND 6 OF POCSO ACT AND SEC.9 OF PROHIBITION OF CHILD MARRIAGE ACT 2006 PENDING ON THE FILE OF ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS COURT CHIKKABALLAPURA IN SPL.S.C.NO.139/2021.

entities.text: ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS COURT CHIKKABALLAPURA
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent-State and perused the material on record.
2.
The de-facto complainant is served with the notice but there is no representation.

3. Charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner/sole accused in connection with crime No.103/2021 of Women Police Station, Chikkaballapura for offences punishable under Sections 363,376(2)(n) of IPC, Sections 4 and 6 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. It is alleged by the prosecution that the petitioner herein kidnapped the minor victim i.e. the daughter of the first informant on 15.09.2021 at about 10.30 a.m. from her village and took her to his house situated in Chintamani Taluk and married her by tying a turmeric thread in a temple and then committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on her from 15.09.2021 to 02.10.2021 and thereby committed the charge sheeted offences.

5. The learned counsel for petitioner would contend that even if the prosecution case is accepted,
then it can be seen that it is a case of love affair as it is evident from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.

He submits that the evidence of the first informant as well as the victim has been recorded and since the petitioner is in judicial custody from 03.10.2021, he may be enlarged on bail by imposing conditions.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned HCGP for respondent/State has opposed the prayer seeking bail by contending that the petitioner has committed a heinous offence against a minor girl and in the event of his release, he may try to influence or threaten her and also flee from justice.
7. I have perused the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as the copy of the deposition of the victim girl recorded before the Trial Court.

Having perused the same, at this stage,
it cannot be said that there is no prima-facie case made out against the petitioner.
Since the trial is in progress, any observations made on merits may prejudice the case of prosecution as well as the defence.
8. Having considered the material on record, I am of the considered view that this is not a fit case to grant bail to the petitioner.
However, considering that the trial is in progress, the learned Sessions Judge is directed to expedite the Trial.
With the above observation, the petition is dismissed.

Sd/-
